The Irish and the heavenly both
Have claimed me, and I keep my oath,
A thousand strings would be too few,
For all the music I can do.

ciphers.hint: A large keyboard instrument with pipes.
poem_stanzas:
A cabinet of pipes and keys,
That breathes a thunder on the breeze,
I fill the church with rolling sound,
From the pedalboard up to the crown.

The bellows and the many stops,
Can whisper low or shake the tops,
The wedding and the funeral know,
The many voices of my row.

ciphers.hint: A round metal plate struck to make a ringing sound.
poem_stanzas:
A polished disc of ringing brass,
That clangs a warning to the mass,
I'm struck or brushed or softly kissed,
And add a glitter none has missed.

Two of us meet with a mighty crash,
And send the orchestra a flash,
A hiss, a shimmer, and a clang,
The brightest of the beats I bang.

ciphers.hint: A small drum with jingling metal discs.
poem_stanzas:
A ring of wood with jingling pairs,
That shakes and rattles everywhere,
I'm held aloft and struck or spun,
A one-hand drum for dance and fun.

The gypsy and the gospel choir,
Both use me to lift the fire,
The little discs that line my frame,
Will jingle at the slightest shake.

ciphers.hint: A group of musical notes sounded together.
poem_stanzas:
Three notes or more, struck all at once,
A single sound that bears a bunch,
The harmony beneath the tune,
That mends the ear and fills the room.

A major one is bright and brave,
A minor one will dig a grave,
The guitarist forms me with a hand,
And I'm the stair on which songs stand.

ciphers.hint: A graceful ballroom dance in triple time.
poem_stanzas:
A dance in three, a turning pair,
That sweeps across the ballroom floor,
One-two-three and one-two-three,
The count that sets the dancers free.

The Viennese once made me grand,
The princes took me by the hand,
A river composer, blue and wide,
Once wrote me for the swirling tide.

ciphers.hint: A soothing song sung to help a child sleep.
poem_stanzas:
A quiet song for closing eyes,
That hushes all the waking cries,
I'm sung in dark and sung in low,
And rock the cradle soft and slow.

The mother and the nurse and moon,
All know the gentle, drowsy tune,
The babe will drift, the eyelids fall,
And I'm the softest song of all.

ciphers.hint: A team sport played with sticks and a puck.
poem_stanzas:
A game on ice, or grass, or field,
With crooked sticks and goals to yield,
I skate and pass and shoot and score,
The crowd will roar and roar for more.

The puck, the ball, the whistle's cry,
The goalie guards what cannot fly,
The team will chase the rubber round,
Until the winning goal is found.

ciphers.hint: A combat sport of punching with padded gloves.
poem_stanzas:
Two fighters circle in a square,
With padded fists and gasping air,
A bell begins and ends the round,
And knocks a body to the ground.

The referee will count to ten,
And separate the charging men,
A jab, a hook, a clinch, a fall,
The oldest duel of them all.

ciphers.hint: The sport of riding ocean waves on a board.
poem_stanzas:
A board, a wave, a balancing man,
Who rides the break as fast as he can,
I paddle out and turn and drop,
And glide until the breakers stop.

The swell is born a thousand miles,
And dies upon the sand in piles,
The rider carves the moving wall,
And tries to keep from taking a fall.

ciphers.hint: The sport of swordplay with slender blades.
poem_stanzas:
A duel with blades of buttoned steel,
A lunge, a parry, and a feel,
White suits and masks and line of strip,
The flicker of a lightning tip.

Three weapons share a different rule,
The foil, the épée, and the sabre's rule,
The first to fifteen points has won,
A sport of courtesy and fun.

ciphers.hint: The sport of shooting arrows with a bow.
poem_stanzas:
A bow of yew, a string, a shaft,
A steady hand and ancient craft,
I draw, I aim, I loose, I fly,
And hit the target by and by.

The battlefield and hunt and game,
All bowed before my pointed aim,
The target stands in rings of gold,
And every arrow's flight is told.

ciphers.hint: A combat sport of grappling and pinning.
poem_stanzas:
A sport of grips and holds and throws,
Where only one of two can pose,
I pin the shoulders to the mat,
And end the match just like that.

The Greek and Roman kinds are old,
The ancient games once gave me gold,
A bout of strength and balance true,
With weight classes to divide us two.

ciphers.hint: A prize awarded to a winner.
poem_stanzas:
A silver cup upon a stand,
That waits for one victorious hand,
I'm polished, heavy, bright, and won,
Then hoisted in the setting sun.

I'm raised above the shouting crowd,
With ribbons wrapped and names endowed,
The winner weeps, the loser sighs,
And I reflect the glistening eyes.

ciphers.hint: A person trained to compete in sports.
poem_stanzas:
A body trained and lean and strong,
That runs and jumps and swims along,
I rise before the dawn to train,
And measure victory by pain.

The stadium will shout my name,
I chase the record and the fame,
The medal and the crowd and sweat,
Are all the life that I have met.

I wear a rough cap but never a crown
I fall from a giant and sleep in the ground
A squirrel will bury me, forget where I lie
And from my small death a forest will rise

My shell is a cup that the oak once held
I am hope in a hard brown case
When winter has stripped the branches bare
I keep the future of the wood in my hand
ciphers.hint: The little capped seed the oak lets fall.

poem_stanzas:
I carry the tide that never rests
Away from the drum that beats in the chest
No bone protects me, I hide deep within
But when I am blocked, the whole body dims

Red is my river, my walls are strong
I weave like branches the whole body long
Feel for my pulse where the wrist is thin
A road of blood, from heart to limb
ciphers.hint: A vessel carrying blood away from the heart.

poem_stanzas:
I tie the muscle fast to the bone
A cord of white where the strength is thrown
I do not move, but I make things move
Stretch me too far and the joint will lose its groove

Achilles bore my famous name
I pull on the lever of every frame
Silent and tough, I hold the joint
The rope that anchors flesh to point
ciphers.hint: Fibrous cord that binds muscle to bone.

poem_stanzas:
I am the dark well at the center of sight
I widen at night and narrow at light
Through me the world pours into the mind
A little black moon of the human kind

When danger comes I grow and stare
When love looks close, I soften there
I am the window's deepest part
The doorway to the soul and heart
ciphers.hint: The opening in the iris that lets in light.

poem_stanzas:
I crack when you clench in anger or play
Four of us wait at the end of the day
I am the joint where the finger bends
A bony hinge where the hand extends

Rap on a door and I take the blow
White and hard when the fists are slow
Line us together across the hand
Count my cousins on fingers you command
ciphers.hint: The joint where a finger meets the hand.

poem_stanzas:
A fringe of dark on the edge of seeing
I keep out the dust from the world of being
I flutter when startled, I rest when you dream
A curtain of hair on a narrow stream

Not on the head, but above the eye
I catch the rain when the storms are nigh
I frame the window where glances are cast
A tiny fence that is built to last
ciphers.hint: One of the short hairs on the eyelid's edge.

poem_stanzas:
Two caves open on the face's hill
Where the breath goes in and the scents spill
I flare in fury, I pinch in cold
A doorway of air that is never sold

Through me comes the rose and the smoke and the sea
Through me the danger of fire finds me
I am a tunnel of warm dark air
The entrance the wind uses unaware
ciphers.hint: Either of the two openings through which you breathe.

poem_stanzas:
I blush for you when the blood runs warm
I rise with a smile and soften in storm
Tears may travel the road down my side
Where kisses are planted and secrets hide

I am the seat of the dimpled grin
The soft round field on the side of the chin
A brush may powder me, a hand may rest
The tender slope of the human face
ciphers.hint: The soft side of the face below the eye.

poem_stanzas:
I am the pillar that bears the weight
The longest bone of the upright gait
I run with the runner, I kneel with the prayer
The strong upper limb that hangs in air

A joint above, a joint below
I swing the leg wherever you go
I hold the power of every leap
A column of flesh the muscles keep
ciphers.hint: The upper part of the leg, above the knee.

poem_stanzas:
I am the blue road on the back of the hand
I bring the blood home across the land
I carry the tired tide back to the heart
A quiet river in the body's chart

Green beneath the pale white skin
I am where the nurse begins
When I am tapped, the red comes out
A returning road without a doubt
ciphers.hint: A vessel that carries blood back toward the heart.

poem_stanzas:
A sliver of silver hung in the dark
A smile with no body, a curve with no mark
I grow and I shrink as the month goes by
A cradle of light in the black of the sky

Born of a circle you cannot see whole
I am the young moon's shining soul
A boat made of light on a dark sea
The oldest lamp watching over me
ciphers.hint: The curved shape of the young moon.

poem_stanzas:
Twice in the year the scales are set
When day and night in balance met
No side wins, the light is even
A truce between the dark and heaven

When spring arrives and autumn too
I mark the turn for me and you
The sun stands over the equator line
And equal hours are yours and mine
ciphers.hint: Either of two yearly times when day and night are equal.

poem_stanzas:
I circle the world and never land
A metal moon made by human hand
I watch the storms and carry the call
A wandering eye that sees it all

I ride above the atmosphere
And send the signal far and clear
Some of my kin are moons of stone
Some are machines that fly alone
ciphers.hint: An object that orbits a larger body.

poem_stanzas:
I am the whole that has no edge
Where every star keeps its pledge
Expanding since the first bright shout
What all of this is really about

Galaxies swim in my deep black sea
I am the sum of all there will be
The void and the lights and the dust between
Everything that has ever been
ciphers.hint: The universe regarded as an ordered whole.

poem_stanzas:
A dead star spins and throws a beam
A lighthouse flashing in a cosmic dream
So regular, so fast, so bright
A heartbeat stolen from the night

I am a corpse of a giant sun
That sweeps the sky with a spinning gun
My radio song is a metronome
Calling the lost and lonely home
ciphers.hint: A rapidly spinning neutron star that emits beams.

poem_stanzas:
The brightest lamp in the oldest night
A furnace burning with ancient light
A galaxy's core in a blinding blaze
Seen across the universe's maze

I shine from the dawn of time
A beacon at the edge of the climb
So far my light is a ghost of then
A candle from where it all began
ciphers.hint: An extremely bright, distant source at a galaxy's core.

poem_stanzas:
I answer the moon and I never ask why
I climb the beach and then I sigh
I pull the whole ocean to and fro
A breathing sea that comes and goes

Twice a day I reach and retreat
I bury the rock and uncover the street
The moon is my master, the wind is my friend
I am the edge of the sea without end
ciphers.hint: The alternate rising and falling of the sea.

poem_stanzas:
A white-hot fork with a thunderous voice
A sudden vein with a burning choice
I split the dark and I strike the tree
A second of fury that sets you free

I am born in the belly of a storm
A crack of light in a monstrous form
Count the seconds to know how far
I am the sky's electric scar
ciphers.hint: A brilliant flash of electricity during a storm.

poem_stanzas:
I am the arm of a silent giant
Reaching for light, forever compliant
Birds build on me, the wind pulls me down
A wooden road above the ground

I fork from the trunk and I never walk
The ribs of a tree in winter's talk
I hold the leaf and I hold the nest
A ladder of wood for the sky's request
ciphers.hint: A limb growing out from the trunk of a tree.

poem_stanzas:
I go where the light can never reach
I drink in the dark from the hidden beach
I hold the giant against the gale
A prisoner deep in a secret jail

Above you see the branches spread
Below I labor in the dark instead
I am the anchor and the thirst
The hidden mouth that feeds the first
ciphers.hint: The part of a plant that grows underground.

poem_stanzas:
I am a promise folded small
A sleeping forest inside a ball
Bury me under, water me well
And I will break from my little shell

I hold tomorrow in my coat
A tiny ship, a living boat
The squirrel and the farmer both want me
The start of every plant and tree
ciphers.hint: The small part from which a new plant grows.

poem_stanzas:
I am a green velvet on the stone
A soft carpet where the damp has grown
I have no flower, I scatter no grain
I clothe the north side of the lane

Follow me when you are lost
I grow on the side that favors the frost
A pillow for the forest floor
A quiet green above the door
ciphers.hint: A small soft green plant of damp, shaded places.

poem_stanzas:
I unroll like a tiny fist
A green feather in the forest mist
I have no blossom, only fronds
That whisper of forgotten ponds

I thrive in the shade of the older trees
I sway in the damp with the oldest breeze
A fossil of a greener time
The lace of the forest in its prime
ciphers.hint: A flowerless plant with feathery fronds.

poem_stanzas:
I climb where I am not wanted
I coil and twist till the wall is haunted
I hold the grape that becomes the wine
A green rope of a creeping design

I will not stand, I will not be straight
I hug the lattice and lie in wait
Give me a trellis, give me a tree
And I will climb to where I want to be
ciphers.hint: A plant that climbs or trails along a support.

poem_stanzas:
I weep by the water with trailing hair
I bend in the wind like a woman in prayer
My branches sweep the river's skin
A green fountain that folds within

I stand at the edge of the quiet lake
I bow and I sigh for sorrow's sake
My leaves are thin as a silver knife
I am the tree of the water of life
ciphers.hint: A water-loving tree with long drooping branches.

poem_stanzas:
I stand in the shallow with a hollow stem
The marsh is my home, the wind is my hem
Music is made when the shepherd cuts me
A pipe for the lips that would set the forest free

I bend with the flood and I rise again
A green spear in the water's domain
I have no flower, I bear no grain
But the marsh is my kingdom and the wind my refrain
ciphers.hint: A tall, hollow-stemmed grass of wet places.

poem_stanzas:
I turn the field to a sea of gold
A bearded army, a hundredfold
Milled to powder and baked to bread
I am the staff that keeps you fed

I bow my head when heavy with grain
I drink the sunshine and I drink the rain
On a summer day the farmers come
To gather the harvest beneath the sun
ciphers.hint: The golden grain from which most bread is made.

poem_stanzas:
I am a field of trees in rows
Where the bee and the blossom come and go
I give the apple, the pear, the plum
A garden of fruit when the harvests come

The farmer prunes me and stakes me straight
I reward his patience and I make him wait
A grove of sweetness on a sunny slope
An annual promise and an annual hope
ciphers.hint: A place where fruit trees are cultivated.

poem_stanzas:
I am a patch the hands have tamed
Where the wild is fenced and the weeds are named
I give the rose and the bean and the beet
A little Eden at the edge of the street

The hoe and the watering can are my friends
I begin where the wilderness ends
I bloom for the patient, I sleep in the frost
A labor of love that is never quite lost
ciphers.hint: A plot of ground where flowers or vegetables are grown.

poem_stanzas:
I am a green cathedral of heat
Where the rain and the vine and the parrot meet
The sun cannot find the floor below
A tangle of life that will not let go

The tiger and the monkey and the snake
Live in the thicket that I make
I am the loudest and densest of woods
Where the wild is wild and the damp is good
ciphers.hint: Dense tangled forest of a hot, rainy region.

poem_stanzas:
I am neither water nor land, but both
A soggy kingdom, a reedy growth
The frog and the heron and the eel call me home
I am the soft green ground where the rushes roam

My breath is a mist and my floor is mud
I am where the river lets go of its flood
Step in and you sink, I am shy of the boot
A wet, quiet place where the wild things root
ciphers.hint: An area of low, wet, soft ground.

poem_stanzas:
I am a mouth in the side of the hill
Dark and hollow and terribly still
The bats hang above and the water drips down
I am the deepest of rooms in the ground

Fire once flickered and painted my wall
When the hunters drew the bison and all
I am older than doors, I am colder than stone
A black empty throat where the earth is alone
ciphers.hint: A large natural hollow in a hillside or cliff.

poem_stanzas:
I am a rock that the river wore down
Smooth in the palm, I have no crown
I skip on the water and sink in the sand
A piece of the mountain shaped by a hand

I began as a boulder, I ended as ball
The waves and the seasons made me small
I rattle in the shallows, I rest on the shore
A tiny stone that was stone before
ciphers.hint: A small, smooth, rounded stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am a million grains of stone
Where the sea and the desert make their throne
I run through your fingers and I hold no form
A shifting floor in the calm and the storm

Castles are built where I lie deep
The tide will flatten them while you sleep
I am the hourglass, I am the shore
The tiny gold that the waves adore
ciphers.hint: Fine, loose grains of worn rock.

poem_stanzas:
I am the dark skin of the earth
Where the sprout is born and the root has birth
I am the worm's home and the farmer's friend
A living blanket that the plough will tend

I am made of rock and rot and rain
I hold the memory of every grain
Tend me and I will feed you well
Neglect me and I am dust and hell
ciphers.hint: The upper layer of earth in which plants grow.

poem_stanzas:
I am earth that was born to be wet
A potter's friend, a sculptor's pet
Bake me in fire and I will be strong
A jug, a bowl, a tile, a song

I am soft in your hands and hard in the kiln
I take the shape of the potter's will
Slick and gray when the river is high
A moldable stone that learns to dry
ciphers.hint: A stiff sticky earth that can be molded and fired.

poem_stanzas:
I am the smallest of crumbs of rock
I ride on the wind and I leave no lock
I settle on shelves and I tickle the nose
A pale gray film where the still air goes

When the broom is busy I fly in the sun
A million tiny motes on the run
I am what is left when the world wears thin
The humble coat of the kin of stone
ciphers.hint: Fine dry particles of earth or other matter.

poem_stanzas:
I am a funnel that drops from the cloud
A twisting rope that is terribly loud
I tear through the town and I lift up the wood
A giant dark finger that means no good

I spin on the plain and I howl like a train
I leave in my wake only ruin and pain
The sky gave me birth and the ground gives me power
A whirling black beast in the heart of the shower
ciphers.hint: A violently rotating column of air.

poem_stanzas:
A white wall walks across the field
And every road is forced to yield
The wind is a blade and the ice is a spear
And you cannot see further than your fear

I bury the fence and I silence the bell
I turn the whole world into a white hell
When I have passed and the morning is clear
The drifts are the castles I leave here
ciphers.hint: A severe snowstorm with strong winds.

poem_stanzas:
I am the rain's shy little brother
I barely wet one and never the other
I drift and I mizzle and I bead on the glass
A fine gray veil where the slow hours pass

The ducks don't mind me, the children don't run
I am the gray that hides the sun
I take my time and I make small pools
A soft wet whisper that the garden loves
ciphers.hint: Light rain falling in very fine drops.

poem_stanzas:
I am a cloud that came down to the ground
A white gray ghost that has swallowed the sound
I hide the lighthouse and I hide the hill
And I make the whole world pale and still

The ships sound their horns to feel their way
Through the wet gray wool of my day
I am the breath of the sea and the moor
A damp white curtain without a door
ciphers.hint: A thick cloud of tiny water droplets near the ground.

poem_stanzas:
I am born in the dark and I die in the dawn
A bead on the leaf, a tear on the lawn
The morning finds me and I disappear
A tiny jewel that the cold night left here

I am not rain and I am not mist
I am the night's gift to the garden and the flower
I glisten on webs, I shine on the thorn
A thousand small mirrors where the cold air goes
ciphers.hint: Tiny drops of moisture that form overnight.

poem_stanzas:
I am the last breath of a dying fire
A glowing eye when the flames climb higher
Orange and soft in the gray of the burned
I keep the heat when the logs are turned

Breathe on me and I will come awake
A little red life for the campfire's sake
I am the spark that refuses to die
The warm red heart of the hearth's goodbye
ciphers.hint: A small piece of glowing coal in a dying fire.

poem_stanzas:
I am what remains when the flame is through
A gray soft powder, a ghost of the flue
I float on the wind and I smudge the hand
A pale reminder of the fire's command

From my dust the garden is fed
I am the quiet after the red
The mountain and the hearth both leave me behind
A soft gray snow of the burned-out kind
ciphers.hint: The powdery residue left after something burns.

poem_stanzas:
I rise from the fire and I smell of the pine
A gray ribbon twisting in a wandering line
I sting in the eye and I blot out the sun
I am the ghost of the burning done

Signal or danger, I speak from the hill
I carry the warning, I carry the chill
Chimneys breathe me into the sky
A drifting veil that can make you cry
ciphers.hint: The visible gray cloud rising from a fire.

poem_stanzas:
I slide down the bank on my belly for fun
I dine on the fish when the day is done
I float on my back in the river's bend
A playful brown swimmer, the water's friend

I live in a holt in the roots of the bank
I am sleek and I am slick and I never am sank
Hold hands with me in the stream
And we will drift like a happy dream
ciphers.hint: A playful, fish-eating mammal of rivers and coasts.

poem_stanzas:
I dig a sett in the dark of the hill
A fortress of tunnels, a burgher's will
Black and white stripes on my grumpy face
I keep to the night and I know my place

I am squat and I am strong and I fear no dog
I bumble through bracken and under the log
The woodsman knows me and leaves me be
A grumpy old resident of the country
ciphers.hint: A burrowing mammal with a black-and-white striped face.

poem_stanzas:
I am a pincushion that walks at night
Rolled in a ball when I take a fright
I wear a coat of a thousand spikes
And I hunt for beetles and worms and the like

The fox may try me but I will not bend
Into a prickly fortress I descend
When the winter comes I sleep till spring
A small brown grump with a thousand sting
ciphers.hint: A small spiny mammal that rolls into a ball.

poem_stanzas:
I leap from the oak to the elm to the roof
My tail is a flag and a parachute proof
I bury the nuts in a hundred spots
And forget where I hid half of my lots

I chatter at dogs from the top of the tree
I scold and I scurry, I am never carefree
When winter comes I dig in the snow
For the dinner I planted so long ago
ciphers.hint: A bushy-tailed tree-climbing rodent that hoards nuts.

poem_stanzas:
I wade in the lake with my great heavy head
I browse on the willow and the lily bed
My antlers are shovels, my shoulders are wide
I am the giant of the northern side

I am tall as a door and I walk through the fog
The wolves keep their distance, the flies are a plague
When the autumn is cold I call to the wood
A long-legged lord of the marsh and the mud
ciphers.hint: A very large northern deer with broad palmate antlers.

poem_stanzas:
I climb the cliff where the grass is thin
I eat the tin can and the thistle and the bin
My beard is a banner, my eyes are strange
I headbutt the fence for the joy of the change

I give the milk and the cheese and the kid
I live on the rock where the farmers forbid
Sure-footed and stubborn, I laugh at the steep
A devilish climber among the woolly sheep
ciphers.hint: A hardy horned farm animal that climbs rocks.

poem_stanzas:
I wear a coat that is warm and white
The farmer shears me at the edge of night
I follow the flock and I never lead
And I eat the meadow and the clover and the weed

Count me to fall asleep at last
The wolf may scare me, I run too fast
My lamb is my joy, my wool is my worth
A woolly cloud that walks the earth
ciphers.hint: A woolly farm animal kept for its fleece.

poem_stanzas:
I am the night in a coat of spots
I climb the tree and I hide the lots
I drag my dinner up out of reach
A silent shadow that the monkeys preach

I am the strongest of the climbing cats
I hunt alone and I leave no tracks
My rosettes are the flowers of the dark
A golden ghost with a silent bark
ciphers.hint: A large spotted wild cat that climbs trees.

poem_stanzas:
I am the fastest thing on four feet
A blur of spots on the plain of heat
Tears run down from the corners of my eyes
And the antelope knows that it is unwise

I do not roar, I purr and I chirp
I trip the swift and I take my grip
I am built like a greyhound, lean and long
A living arrow, a streak of song
ciphers.hint: The fastest land animal, a slender spotted cat.

poem_stanzas:
I am a cat that is black as the pit
My scream in the night makes the jungle sit
I am the shadow of the shadowy wood
The master of silence, the hunter of blood

Some call me the leopard's twin in the gloom
I am the darkness that the moonlight lets in
I move without sound and I strike without fear
A black flowing river, the end of the deer
ciphers.hint: A large black wild cat; a melanistic big cat.

poem_stanzas:
I am a steed in a striped disguise
A maze of black on the plain of size
My stripes are as unique as a fingerprint
And the lion must pick which one to hint

I graze with the wildebeest in the herd
I am not the wildest, I am not the bird
My coat is the dazzle that confuses the fly
A walking barcode beneath the sky
ciphers.hint: An African wild horse with black-and-white stripes.

poem_stanzas:
I look down on the world from a tower of neck
I browse the top leaves of the tree that I pick
My tongue is long and my spots are brown
I am the tallest lady in town

My heart is the size of a football, they say
To pump the blood the long, long way
I walk like a camel and I run like the wind
The lookout of the savanna kind
ciphers.hint: A very tall African mammal with a long spotted neck.

poem_stanzas:
I carry the desert on my back
I store my dinner in a humped sack
My feet are wide and my lashes long
And I cross the dunes like a ships' song

I drink my fill and I travel for days
Through the burning sand and the dusty haze
The desert is my ship and I am its crew
A patient wanderer of the sun-bleached hue
ciphers.hint: A humped desert animal used as a pack beast.

poem_stanzas:
I eat a forest of bamboo
The black on my eyes is a mask for you
I am round and I roll and I sit and I chew
And the whole wide world comes to look at me

I am black and white and I am never in a rush
I crush the cane in my jaw's soft crush
My cub is tiny, pink and blind
A bamboo bear of the gentlest kind
ciphers.hint: A black-and-white bamboo-eating bear of China.

poem_stanzas:
I carry my baby in a pocket of fur
I box with my paws and I kick at the spur
I hop on two legs with a powerful tail
And I bound across the bush like a gale

I am the emblem of the southern land
I stand on my tail and I do not need a hand
My joey peeks from the pouch I own
A hopping giant of the dry outback
ciphers.hint: A marsupial that hops on strong hind legs.

poem_stanzas:
I am the biggest bird that cannot fly
I run on two legs with my head held high
I kick like a horse and I swallow the stone
And I lay the largest egg that is known

The sand and the savanna are my home
I strut with my feathers like a feathered comb
Do not believe that I hide my head
The fastest thing on two legs instead
ciphers.hint: A large flightless bird of African plains.

poem_stanzas:
I am a walking fan of a hundred eyes
I spread my feathers to hypnotize
My scream is a shriek, my walk is a strut
I am the vainest bird in the hut

The blue and the green and the gold all shine
When I open my tail in a great design
The ladies are plain, but I am the show
A proud feathered rainbow whose colors glow
ciphers.hint: A male bird famous for its huge colorful tail fan.

poem_stanzas:
I wear the colors of the jungle's crown
Red and green and blue and brown
I crack the nut with my curved beak
And I copy the words that the humans speak

I sit on a shoulder and I shriek and I talk
I waddle on the perch and I never take a walk
I live as long as a person may
The loud bright mimic of the leafy day
ciphers.hint: A brightly colored bird that can mimic speech.

poem_stanzas:
I am the gray bird of the city square
I peck at the crumbs and I flutter and stare
I carry a message across the war
And I always find my way back to the door

I am the dove of the gentle kind
I bob my head as I walk and I mind
I coo on the ledge and I strut on the ground
A city commuter without a sound
ciphers.hint: A plump gray city bird, once used as a messenger.

poem_stanzas:
I am small and brown and everywhere
I bathe in the dust and I eat the fare
The hawk may hunt me, the cat may creep
But I am the bird that the city keeps

I hop on the pavement and I chirp on the wire
I build a nest in the eaves and the briar
I am common and humble and hard to see
But the world would be quieter without me
ciphers.hint: A small brown bird common in towns and gardens.

poem_stanzas:
I wear a breast of rusty red
I hop on the lawn where the worms are fed
I sing in the winter when others are gone
And I follow the spade from dusk to dawn

I am the gardener's friend and the Christmas bird
I cock my head at the smallest word
I am round and I am bold and I am often seen
A little red shield on a field of green
ciphers.hint: A small bird with a red breast, seen in gardens.

poem_stanzas:
I stand like a statue on one thin leg
Watching the water, patient as the dreg
I spear the fish with a dagger beak
And I fly with a slow and a heavy creak

I am gray and tall on the river's edge
I nest in the tops of the highest tree
The fishermen fear me, the frogs all flee
A hunched old statue that waits by the sea
ciphers.hint: A tall, long-legged bird that hunts fish in shallows.

poem_stanzas:
I glide on the lake like a white ship
With my neck in a curve and my orange lip
The ugly duckling grew into me
And I mate for life on the silent sea

I am graceful and cold and I hiss if you press
I wear a gown of snowy dress
The queen of the water, the pride of the pond
A silent white sail with a neck so long
ciphers.hint: A large white water bird with a long curved neck.

poem_stanzas:
I honk in the sky in a V of wings
I fly with the seasons and I follow the springs
I guard the farm with a hiss and a peck
And I lay an egg that is bigger than a speck

My feathers are the quill and the down
The pillow and the pen of the town
I waddle and I paddle and I graze on the green
A noisy traveler of the sky unseen
ciphers.hint: A large waterfowl with a loud honk.

poem_stanzas:
I am black as coal and clever as a thief
I solve the puzzle and I cause the grief
I croak from the tower and the gallows tree
And the poets have made a legend of me

I am bigger than my cousin and I fly alone
I imitate the wolf and the human's tone
Nevermore is the word they gave
A glossy black omen above the grave
ciphers.hint: A large glossy black bird known for its intelligence.

poem_stanzas:
I dress in black and white and blue
I chatter and I steal the shiny from you
I build a dome of sticks and thorns
And I scold the world on the frosty morns

One for sorrow, two for joy
I am the bird the superstitions employ
I am bold and I am loud and I am never shy
A thief with a jewel in its eye
ciphers.hint: A black-and-white bird known for collecting shiny objects.

poem_stanzas:
I lie on the ice with a great mustache
I dive for the clam in the cold gray wash
My tusks are long and my hide is thick
And I haul my bulk on the floes that stick

I bellow from the shore of the frozen sea
My whiskers feel for the dinner in the lee
I am the giant of the Arctic sprawl
The mountain of blubber that the storms call
ciphers.hint: A large tusked Arctic sea mammal.

poem_stanzas:
I balance a ball on my whiskered nose
I bask on the rock where the cold tide flows
I bark in the pool and I clap my flipper
A slick gray swimmer, a fish's skipper

I am the dog of the sea to the eye
I swim like a shadow and I haul out dry
My coat is the gray of the harbor stone
A round-eyed wanderer of the cold sea zone
ciphers.hint: A sleek sea mammal that rests on rocks and ice.

poem_stanzas:
I dig through the dark with my shovel hands
I am blind as a stone in the underground lands
I leave little hills where the garden was
The velvet of the soil is my house

I eat the worm and I never see the sky
I am a black soft mystery passing by
Touch me and I will vanish below
A tiny blind miner in the earth's dark glow
ciphers.hint: A small burrowing mammal that lives underground.

poem_stanzas:
I bask on the stone and I snap the fly
I shed my skin when the sun is high
I drop my tail to escape the cat
And grow a new one, imagine that

I creep on four feet through the desert heat
I flick my tongue at the things I eat
I am cold in the morning and quick in the noon
A little armored dragon under the moon
ciphers.hint: A scaly four-legged reptile that basks in the sun.

poem_stanzas:
I rise from the basket when the flute begins
I spread my hood and I sway and I grin
My bite is a needle of venom and dread
And the charmer is safe by a thread

I am the serpent of the king and the tomb
I glide through the grass and I seal the doom
I strike like a whip and I hiss like a kettle
The jewel of the jungle, the deadly petal
ciphers.hint: A venomous snake that spreads a hood when threatened.

poem_stanzas:
I walk on the floor of the cold blue deep
In armor of red that the boiling will steep
I hold up my claws like a knight of the sea
And I scuttle in the dark where the fish are free

I have ten legs and I taste with my feet
I hide in the rocks and I pinch and I meet
I turn to the color of sunset when cooked
A sea-dragon in a shell that is hooked
ciphers.hint: A clawed sea creature with a hard shell.

poem_stanzas:
I am a rough stone that lives in the bay
I filter the water and I shut when you play
Inside me a treasure is slowly grown
A pearl for the crown of a queen on her throne

I have two shells and a soft gray heart
I cling to the reef and I play my part
The knife must open me for the feast
A homely rock with a jewel at least
ciphers.hint: A rough-shelled sea creature that can yield a pearl.

poem_stanzas:
I am a bell of Jell-O that swims
With a hundred threads on my ghostly rims
I glow in the dark and I sting like fire
And I drift with the current, never tire

I have no brain and I have no bone
A bloom of the sea that drifts alone
The turtle eats me and closes its eyes
A floating umbrella of the warming tides
ciphers.hint: A soft, umbrella-shaped sea creature that can sting.

poem_stanzas:
I swim upright with a horse's head
I curl my tail round the coral bed
The father carries the babies, it's true
A tiny dragon in a coat of sea-blue

I have a snout and a crown and a fin
I hover and I hide when the tide comes in
I hold to the weed with my gripping tail
A slow little knight in a watery vale
ciphers.hint: A small fish with a horse-like head and curled tail.

poem_stanzas:
I march in a line and I carry the crumb
I live in a hill with a queen and a drum
I lift ten times my weight in the sand
And I find my way home with a touch of the hand

I never sleep and I never rest
I farm the aphid and I raid the nest
I am small but I am legion and I am strong
A little black worker the whole day long
ciphers.hint: A small social insect that lives in colonies.

poem_stanzas:
I dance to tell where the flowers are
I hum in the hive and I fly afar
I carry the pollen and I make the sweet
And I die with my sting at the end of my feat

I have a queen and a comb of cells
I guard the gold where the honey dwells
I wear black and yellow to warn you away
A buzzing gardener of the summer day
ciphers.hint: A striped insect that makes honey.

poem_stanzas:
I am the cousin of the butterfly
But I fly at night when the sun has gone by
I circle the lamp in a dusty gown
And I blend with the bark when I settle down

I am pale and plump and I love the dark
I leave a hole in your favorite coat
I come from a cocoon of silk
A quiet gray ghost that thinks light is milk
ciphers.hint: A dull-colored insect that flies chiefly at night.

poem_stanzas:
I wear a shell of polished black
I carry my armor on my back
I roll the ball of the dung uphill
And I work in the heat with a stubborn will

I am the largest family of them all
I crawl on the leaf and I climb the wall
I have wings beneath my case of sheen
The most successful insect ever seen
ciphers.hint: An insect with hard wing cases covering its back.

poem_stanzas:
I tunnel the soil and I make it sweet
I have no eyes and I have no feet
I eat my way through the garden's ground
And the robin pulls me when I am found

I live in the dark and I hate the sun
I am soft and pink and I am never done
I turn the dead leaf into the loam
A living plough in the earth's dark home
ciphers.hint: A long soft-bodied creature that lives in soil.

poem_stanzas:
I am a bulb in a papery coat
Peel me and I will make you cry in the throat
I layer the soup and I flavor the stew
A pungent ball that the kitchen will use

I grow in the ground with a green top
I make the eyes water and the tongue pop
I am brown or white or red as a ruby
The teary heart of the savory duty
ciphers.hint: A round vegetable with layered skin that can make you cry.

poem_stanzas:
I am a head of leaves wound tight
A green ball of the garden's light
The sauerkraut and the coleslaw are mine
And the winter soup that the poor recline

Peel me and the layers go on and on
A giant bud that the frost cannot con
I feed the farm and I keep through the cold
A humble green ball worth more than gold
ciphers.hint: A round vegetable with thick, densely packed leaves.

poem_stanzas:
I am orange and round and I grow from a vine
At Halloween I leer from the line
I become a coach when the magic is cast
And a pie when the autumn is past

I am the biggest fruit in the patch
The candle inside me makes faces hatch
I feed the feast at Thanksgiving too
The lantern of autumn, the color of brew
ciphers.hint: A large orange squash carved at Halloween.

poem_stanzas:
I am the king of the tropical fruit
Golden and sweet from the tree at the root
I am orange within and green without
A taste of the sun when the summer is out

I grow where the monsoon and the sunshine reign
A golden cheek on a slender cane
The juice runs down to the elbow and chin
A luscious globe of the tropics within
ciphers.hint: A sweet golden tropical fruit with a large stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am fuzzy and round with a blush on my skin
A soft golden sun with a stone deep within
I drip down the chin in the heat of July
A sweet summer treat that the wasps all try

I hang on the bough of the orchard wall
I ripen and soften and then I fall
My flesh is the color of dawn and of jam
A tender ripe globe in the palm of your hand
ciphers.hint: A soft, fuzzy fruit with a large stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am a small red heart on a stem
A jewel of summer, a bright little gem
I hang in a pair and I beckon the bird
And I top the sundae, the sweetest of word

I bloom in the spring in a cloud of pink
I ripen in June at the orchard's brink
Inside me a stone and around me a skin
A sweet little marble that invites you in
ciphers.hint: A small round red fruit with a single stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am a wrinkly brain in a shell
I crack with a hammer and fall where I fell
I dress the salad and top the cake
A wrinkled gold that the squirrels take

I grow in a green husk on the bough
I am rich and bitter and good for the heart
I look like the mind of a very old tree
A fortress of ridges that holds the meat
ciphers.hint: A hard-shelled nut with a wrinkled kernel.

poem_stanzas:
I am the crisp green leaf of the bed
A ruffled collar around the bread
I crunch in the salad and cool the taco
A watery ruffle, a green tobacco

I grow in a hurry and bolt in the heat
I wrap the burger and cool the meat
I am pale in the middle and green at the edge
A leafy umbrella for the garden's wedge
ciphers.hint: A green salad vegetable with crisp leaves.

poem_stanzas:
I am a heavy green ball in the field
A cool sweet water my flesh will yield
I am pink or orange or golden within
A summer refreshment that beats the gin

I grow on a vine and I ripen in the sun
A giant for the table when the day is done
My seeds are a string and my rind is a shell
A juicy globe with a story to tell
ciphers.hint: A large juicy fruit with a hard rind and many seeds.

poem_stanzas:
I am a small purple globe of juice
A sweet-tart treasure that hangs on the noose
I dry into a prune in the sun
And the pudding and the jam are never done

I bloom early white on the orchard tree
A velvety fruit that the wasps all see
My stone is a point and my skin is a bloom
A purple delight in the autumn's room
ciphers.hint: A small purple fruit with smooth skin and a stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am a nut in a pitted shell
A tear-shaped treat where the blossoms fell
I flavor the marzipan and the milk
A pale brown kernel as soft as silk

I grow on a tree of pink in the spring
I ripen in the heat and I am the king
Of the nutty and the sweet and the frangipane
A delicate drop of the orchard's rain
ciphers.hint: An oval nut with a pale brown kernel.

poem_stanzas:
I am not a nut but I wear the name
I grow in a shell on a legume frame
I go with the jelly and the salty snack
A little brown pod that the elephants crack

I bury my flower and I fruit below
A curious habit that few plants know
I am roasted and ground into butter and oil
A humble legume of the southern soil
ciphers.hint: An edible seed that ripens underground in a pod.

poem_stanzas:
I am the grain of the flooded field
A billion bowls are from me filled
I am white or brown and I steam in the pot
A tiny white seed that feeds the lot

I grow in the water in terraced stairs
I am the staple of a thousand prayers
I am the food of half of the world
A patient white grain in a green unfurled
ciphers.hint: A white grain that is a staple food for much of the world.

poem_stanzas:
I am a long strip of dough in the bowl
I curl on the fork and I comfort the soul
I come from Italy, Japan, and the East
A slippery ribbon at the end of the feast

I am boiled and I am fried and I am tossed
From ramen to lasagna I am never lost
I am the strand and the spoon is my friend
A wiggly rope that has no end
ciphers.hint: A strip or tube of pasta or dough.

poem_stanzas:
I am bread that has met the flame
Brown and crisp and never the same
I pop from the slot when the morning is gray
And I hold the butter and jam of the day

I am warm and I crackle and I smell of the grill
The cheese will melt on me and spill
I am the soldier for the soft-boiled egg
A golden slice with a crunchy leg
ciphers.hint: Sliced bread browned by heat.

poem_stanzas:
Long and curved, I cage the breath,
A dozen pairs from throat to base;
I arch above the beating flesh
And shield the seat of life from harm.

I move a little when you breathe,
A basket woven out of bone;
The smallest pair sit at the top,
And all the rest hang down below.
ciphers.hint: One of the curved bones that form the chest cage.

poem_stanzas:
I hinge below the silent nose,
I hold the teeth and shape the face;
I open wide for food and song,
And close with blunt and grinding might.

Two of us exist, above and low,
The lower one does all the work;
The serpent's opens past belief,
And mine can drop in dull surprise.
ciphers.hint: The hinged structure that holds the lower teeth and shapes the mouth.

poem_stanzas:
I stand apart, a stubby one,
The shortest of the five I know;
I turn and grip and press and pinch,
The only one who meets his friends.

Without me you could hold no cup,
No hammer, pen, or apple core;
I give the hand its human skill,
Opposing all the rest to hold.
ciphers.hint: The short, thick first digit of the hand.

poem_stanzas:
I bend the leg and bear the weight,
A hinge that knocks when you run;
I wear a cap of sliding bone
And scar the child who falls on stone.

I genuflect in prayer and dance,
I jerk when struck, a doctor's test;
The oldest joint to feel the years,
The bane of every climbing stair.
ciphers.hint: The joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

poem_stanzas:
I am the flatland of the hand,
The place a fortune-teller reads;
I cup the water, smooth the hair,
I clap in joy and sting in slap.

My lines are mapped by every fate,
The lifeline, heartline, head all cross;
The fingers sprout along my edge,
And I can hold a world of things.
ciphers.hint: The inner surface of the hand between wrist and fingers.

poem_stanzas:
I am the narrow hourglass,
The hinge between the chest and hip;
A belt goes round me, tight or loose,
And dancers hold me as they turn.

I take the name of what I cinch,
The middle that the fashions change;
I am the dip above the curve,
The sash's home, the girdle's mark.
ciphers.hint: The part of the body between the ribs and the hips.

poem_stanzas:
I am the shelf beneath the mouth,
The ledge that juts to make a face;
I tremble when you try not to cry,
And beard and dimple make their home.

I point the profile out to sea,
I tuck beneath a lifted smile;
I am the dock where speech sets sail,
The lower edge of every word.
ciphers.hint: The protruding lower part of the face below the mouth.

poem_stanzas:
I am the field above the brows,
Where thought is written in a line;
I take the kiss of love and death,
The crown of worry and of sweat.

I glisten when the fever burns,
I wrinkle up with age and care;
The hair begins where I leave off,
And horns of anger sprout beneath.
ciphers.hint: The part of the face above the eyes and below the hair.

poem_stanzas:
I bulge behind the lower leg,
The muscle made by many steps;
I take my name from what I am
In younger cattle, sleek and young.

I ache the day you climb a hill,
I cramp and knot and stretch and burn;
The runner knows me, the dancer too,
The second word for baby cow.
ciphers.hint: The fleshy back part of the lower leg.

poem_stanzas:
I am the pivot of the stride,
The ball that swings the leg along;
A child is set upon my shelf,
And fashion measures me for cloth.

I lead the dress, I sway the walk,
A joint with socket, deep and round;
I wear the belt of every dance
And break in age when bones grow thin.
ciphers.hint: The joint at the top of the leg, or the side of the body below the waist.

poem_stanzas:
I walk askance, a sideways knight,
With armor red and claws that pinch;
I scavenge beaches, scuttle dark,
And hide in shells of other folk.

I dine on rot and come in tides,
The moon commands my armored march;
I am the sign when summer comes,
A sideways walker of the sand.
ciphers.hint: A coastal creature with a hard shell and pincers that walks sideways.

poem_stanzas:
I carry my house upon my back,
I leave a silver trail behind;
I move so slowly that the grass
Can grow before I reach the wall.

I have two horns that feel the world,
I vanish when the salt is cast;
The garden hates me, the bird adores,
A curled and patient wanderer.
ciphers.hint: A slow creature with a spiral shell on its back.

poem_stanzas:
I am a rocket of the deep,
With ten soft arms and ink to hide;
I jet away in sudden fright,
And vanish in a cloud of black.

I have a beak within my arms,
I feed the whale, the bigger fish;
The menu calls me calamari,
A torpedo of the ocean dark.
ciphers.hint: A sea creature with a long body, arms, and ink; food for whales.

poem_stanzas:
I have eight arms and no bones at all,
I pour through gaps a flowing ghost;
I change my skin to match the rock,
And jet a fog to blind the shark.

I open jars and solve the maze,
Three hearts beat within my head;
I taste the world with every limb,
A clever shape-shifter of the sea.
ciphers.hint: A soft sea creature with eight arms and no skeleton.

poem_stanzas:
I wear the shape of a fallen star,
Five arms or more around a hub;
I creep on thousands of tiny feet,
And open shells to eat them whole.

I can lose a limb and grow it back,
I prize the oyster from its rock;
I am no fish, though so they call,
A slow flower of the tidal pool.
ciphers.hint: A sea animal shaped like a star with five or more arms.

poem_stanzas:
I am two shells with a hinge between,
I burrow down in sand and mud;
I sip the sea and filter food,
And snap me shut when danger comes.

I stand upon the mudflats wide,
I squirt the stranger who steps too near;
The chowder that the people love
Is made from me the whole world round.
ciphers.hint: A burrowing sea animal with two hinged shells.

poem_stanzas:
I fly at night on leathern wings,
I hang by day in caves and eaves;
I weave the dark with unheard calls,
And catch the moth in mid-flight air.

I am no bird, though I take the sky,
I sleep upside and groom my fur;
The tale of Dracula is mine to rue,
A winged and shadow-hunted thing.
ciphers.hint: A flying mammal active at night that hunts using echolocation.

poem_stanzas:
I am small and grey and quick of foot,
I steal the crumb and dread the cat;
My ears are round, my whiskers twitch,
I nest in walls and whisper late.

I am a classic terror to the house,
I take the cheese and spring the trap;
The field and town both know my tribe,
A tiny tenant of the floor.
ciphers.hint: A small grey rodent with a long tail.

poem_stanzas:
I am the bigger cousin of the mouse,
With scaly tail and cunning mind;
I swim, I climb, I gnaw the rope,
I follow ships to every port.

I empty grain and spread the plague,
The black death rode upon my back;
I learn the maze and dodge the trap,
An unwanted guest in every town.
ciphers.hint: A large gnawing rodent with a long tail.

poem_stanzas:
I am long and slim and fierce for size,
I slip through tunnels, hunt by scent;
I take the vole and raid the nest,
And wear a coat of summer brown.

I turn all white when snows arrive,
I twist and writhe and never quit;
The idiom keeps me in a phrase
For one who wriggles out of blame.
ciphers.hint: A small, slender, carnivorous mammal with a long body.

poem_stanzas:
I am the patient, long-eared one,
The cross upon my shoulders worn;
I carry loads on stony paths,
And bray when I am left alone.

I am the beast of poorer folk,
The mare's plain kin, the stubborn friend;
A symbol of the fool, and half
The parent pair of the weary mule.
ciphers.hint: A domesticated animal like a small horse with long ears.

poem_stanzas:
I am the child of two unlike,
A horse and one with longer ears;
I work the mine and tread the mill,
And keep the patience of my dam.

I cannot breed, or rarely so,
A sterile bridge of blood and toil;
The farmer and the miner know
My stubborn strength on rocky roads.
ciphers.hint: The sterile offspring of a horse and a donkey.

poem_stanzas:
I am the male of horn and might,
I paw the earth and snort the air;
The matador still fears my charge,
And on the farm I sire the herd.

I bear the sign of markets rising,
My neck is ringed with muscle thick;
The red cloth only makes me mad—
Or so the stories all maintain.
ciphers.hint: The adult male of cattle.

poem_stanzas:
I am of the high and windy hills,
I spit when I am over-proud;
I carry packs on mountain trails
And give my wool for woven cloth.

I live where thin air bites the lung,
Andean roads are mine to tread;
The tourist meets me, tame and calm,
A cousin of the camel's line.
ciphers.hint: A South American pack animal related to the camel.

poem_stanzas:
I am the thunder of the plains,
A mountain wrapped in shaggy hide;
I once was millions, now a few,
My hump is king of the grassland wide.

I lower horns and shake the dust,
The prairie trembled at my herd;
The rifle thinned my mighty tribes,
But I remain, a shaggy wall.
ciphers.hint: A large shaggy humped wild ox of North America.

poem_stanzas:
I wear a horn upon my nose,
A tank of hide, a living wall;
I charge the jeep and flip the car,
And hardly see, for my eyes are weak.

I am the grey and armored one,
The second largest beast on land;
The bird rides on my back and picks
The ticks that plague my folded skin.
ciphers.hint: A large thick-skinned African animal with a horn on its nose.

poem_stanzas:
I am a river horse of bulk,
I yawn a cavern of a mouth;
I sweat a red and oily sheen,
And walk the bottom of the lake.

I laze in water all the day,
And graze by night on river grass;
My calves are born beneath the stream,
A boulder of the muddy pool.
ciphers.hint: A large African animal that lives in rivers and has a huge mouth.

poem_stanzas:
I am the giant of the forest green,
I beat my chest and guard my clan;
I eat the leaf and shoot and stem,
And knuckle-walk the leafy floor.

I share the blood of humankind,
The largest of the living apes;
My silver back commands the troop,
A gentle king of the mountain mist.
ciphers.hint: The largest living ape, a powerful African forest primate.

poem_stanzas:
I am a pocket of a pet,
I stuff my cheeks and run a wheel;
I hoard the seed in burrowed rooms,
And sleep the day, awake by night.

I am small and round and soft,
I wash my face with tiny paws;
The child adores me, cage and all,
A furry miller of the night.
ciphers.hint: A small furry rodent often kept as a pet, with cheek pouches.

poem_stanzas:
I bear a dome of patterned shell,
I walk so slow the hare may nap;
I live a century or more,
And draw my head in when you knock.

I am the land-dweller of my kind,
My cousin swims and I do not;
The fable made me beat the hare,
A patient plodder of the grass.
ciphers.hint: A slow-moving land reptile with a hard domed shell.

poem_stanzas:
I am the morning and the evening star,
The brightest jewel of the sky;
I wear a veil of burning cloud,
And turn the wrong way as I spin.

I am the goddess's own name,
The hottest world, the second from the sun;
A furnace wrapped in sulphur bright,
The love-star of the twilight hour.
ciphers.hint: The second planet from the sun, the brightest in our sky.

poem_stanzas:
I am the red one of the wanderers,
My rust is iron, my air is thin;
I hold the tallest mount of all,
And channels carved by vanished floods.

I am the war-god of the old,
My moons are captured, small and scared;
The rovers crawl across my dust,
The fourth bright light in the nightly march.
ciphers.hint: The fourth planet from the sun, known as the red planet.

poem_stanzas:
I am the giant of the planets,
A ball of gas without a floor;
I wear a spot that is a storm
That rages wider than the earth.

I hold a court of many moons,
The largest king of all the sky;
I spin in ten short hours and bulge,
The thunder god's enormous throne.
ciphers.hint: The largest planet in the solar system, marked by a great red spot.

poem_stanzas:
I am the swiftest of the wanderers,
The nearest to the burning sun;
I have no air, I scorch and freeze,
My day is longer than my year.

I am the god of trade and thieves,
The smallest planet, bare and grey;
I race around the sun so fast
That I outrun the morning light.
ciphers.hint: The smallest planet and the nearest to the sun.

poem_stanzas:
I am the farthest of the eight,
A blue and windy, freezing world;
I wear the trident's name,
And winds on me outrun all sound.

I was found by mathematics first,
Before the glass could point my way;
I am the deep sea-god of the sky,
The last great planet of the sun.
ciphers.hint: The eighth and farthest planet from the sun.

poem_stanzas:
I am the small and icy one,
Once counted ninth, then set aside;
I ride beyond the giant worlds
And wear the name of the underworld.

I have a heart of frozen plain,
My moon is almost half my size;
The vote demoted me one day,
A dwarf among the distant dark.
ciphers.hint: A dwarf planet beyond Neptune, once called the ninth planet.

poem_stanzas:
I am the death-cry of a giant,
A star that tears itself apart;
I blaze as bright as all the rest,
Then fade within a month or two.

I forge the gold and silver dust,
I seed the space with heavy stone;
The Chinese wrote of me at noon,
A light that outshone the day.
ciphers.hint: A colossal stellar explosion that briefly outshines an entire galaxy.

poem_stanzas:
I am a stone that fell from heaven,
A traveler from the belt of rock;
I burn across the startled night
And strike the earth and make a pit.

I am the remnant that survives
The fiery passage of the air;
The museum keeps me under glass,
A visitor from outer space.
ciphers.hint: A space rock that survives its fall through the atmosphere to hit the ground.

poem_stanzas:
I am the gnawing in the chest,
The sleepless turning of the night;
I whisper all the things that might,
And make the smallest worry vast.

I live in waiting rooms and exams,
I drum the fingers, bite the nail;
I am the future's shadow cast
Upon a mind that cannot rest.
ciphers.hint: A feeling of worry and unease about what may happen.

poem_stanzas:
I am the surface of the lake
When not a breath of wind has stirred;
The eye of every raging storm,
The pause between the beat of waves.

The sailor prays for me at sea,
The mother sings me to her child;
I am the quiet after tears,
The still and deep and patient peace.
ciphers.hint: A state of peace and freedom from agitation.

poem_stanzas:
I am the shout that greets the win,
The rising toast, the happy clap;
I lift the room and light the face,
And drive the dreary out of doors.

I am the season's greeting word,
The comfort of a fire and friend;
The cup raised high, the song begun,
A warm and bright and social mood.
ciphers.hint: A mood of joy, optimism, and encouragement.

poem_stanzas:
I am the cold that comes before,
The shadow at the top of the stair;
The thing that waits behind the door,
The weight that settles on the breast.

I have no shape and yet I loom,
I turn the brave man's blood to ice;
I am the fear of what will come,
The night before the battle's dawn.
ciphers.hint: A great fear or apprehension of something about to happen.

poem_stanzas:
I am the heat that blinds the eye,
The bull that sees the crimson cloth;
I clench the fist and grind the tooth,
And afterwards I bring the shame.

I am the storm-god's painted face,
The avengers chased the guilty man;
I burn so hot and die so cold,
The anger that has lost its rein.
ciphers.hint: Wild, uncontrolled anger.

poem_stanzas:
I am the giggle and the grin,
The child who spins with pure delight;
I am the chorus of the crowd,
The mischief twinkle in the eye.

I am the song the children sing,
A merry name for mirth and joy;
I bubble up without a cause,
The lightness of a happy heart.
ciphers.hint: Great delight; open and joyful mirth.

poem_stanzas:
I am the fire that asks no reason,
The cold that freezes out the love;
I nurse the grudge and feed the war,
And teach the hand to strike the friend.

I am the opposite of what is kind,
The poison in the family tree;
The proverb bids me conquer all,
Yet I devour the one who holds.
ciphers.hint: An intense dislike or hostility toward someone.

poem_stanzas:
I am the green-eyed one who keeps
The ledger of another's joy;
I count the gifts and weigh the praise,
And find my own too small to bear.

I gnaw the lover and the friend,
I make a prison of a trust;
The name of a god's fierce wife
Is buried in the sound of me.
ciphers.hint: A resentful feeling of envy toward another's advantages.

poem_stanzas:
I am a small and golden globe,
A cousin of the peach and plum;
My skin is down, my heart is stone,
I dry into a wrinkled sweet.

I bloom upon a spreading tree,
I ripen in the summer sun;
The jam and brandy both are mine,
A velvet sun of the orchard row.
ciphers.hint: A small orange-yellow fruit like a peach, with a stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am a tiny indigo bead,
I grow on low and wiry bush;
I stain the tongue and sweet the cake,
And hide beneath the leaves in troops.

The bear and bird and child all seek
My little drum of purple juice;
The muffin and the pie are mine,
A handful of the summer wood.
ciphers.hint: A small dark blue berry that grows on low bushes.

poem_stanzas:
I am the crunch of water green,
A bundle of pale and ribbed stalks;
I come with wings and dip and salt,
And fill the soup with humble scent.

I grow in trenches, bleached and mild,
My leaves are bitter, thrown away;
The diet's friend, the rabbit's joy,
A brittle staff of the garden bed.
ciphers.hint: A crisp green vegetable with long ribbed stalks.

poem_stanzas:
I am the bitter seed of a tree,
The drink of gods in Aztec gold;
I am ground and pressed and sweetened white,
And turn to bars and steaming cups.

I come from pods upon the trunk,
I am fermented, dried, and roasted dark;
The chocolate and the truffle owe
Their deep and midnight sweetness to me.
ciphers.hint: The powdered seed of a tropical tree, used to make chocolate.

poem_stanzas:
I stand in ranks in summer fields,
A golden soldier with a tassel;
My kernels hide in rows on rows,
And silk the color of a maid's hair.

I pop and grind and sweeten bread,
The cob is mine when I am shorn;
The field of me is called an ear,
The autumn's yellow, tall and rough.
ciphers.hint: A tall cereal plant with yellow kernels growing on a cob.

poem_stanzas:
I am cool and green and mostly water,
A trailing vine of prickly leaf;
I dress the salad and the dip,
And make a pickle in the brine.

I hang upon a climbing stem,
I crunch and freshen and refresh;
The sandwich and the Greek dish know
My mild and watery, seedy flesh.
ciphers.hint: A long green vegetable with mild, watery flesh, often pickled.

poem_stanzas:
I am a teardrop, purple-dark,
I hide a thousand tiny seeds;
I grow upon a broad rough leaf,
And ripen in the burning sun.

The wasp and I have a strange bond,
I sweeten cakes and pair with cheese;
The prophet cursed my barren tree,
A honeyed purse of the ancient world.
ciphers.hint: A soft, sweet pear-shaped fruit full of tiny seeds.

poem_stanzas:
I am a giant of the citrus clan,
My skin is thick with bitter pith;
I split in halves like a sunrise,
My segments blush and tart and sting.

I come with diet, spoon, and knife,
I bite the tongue and wake the mouth;
A breakfast fruit of yellow rind,
The bitter-sweet of the morning table.
ciphers.hint: A large round citrus fruit with tart, pink or yellow flesh.

poem_stanzas:
I am the fruit that met the sugar,
I boil, I set, I seal in glass;
I spread on toast and fill the tart,
And sweeten winter from a jar.

I am a traffic snarl as well,
A pickle and a scrape and squeeze;
But mostly I am breakfast's friend,
A sticky jewel of the pantry shelf.
ciphers.hint: A sweet spread made by boiling fruit with sugar.

poem_stanzas:
I am a small and vivid green,
A citrus cousin, sharp and tart;
I wake the drink and cure the fish,
And dye the pie a wicked green.

I am the color and the fruit,
The builder's powder and the tree;
The sailor took me round the world
To keep the sickness from the crew.
ciphers.hint: A small green citrus fruit with sour juice.

poem_stanzas:
I rise in damp and shaded places,
A stalk with an umbrella hat;
I am the fairy's throne and table,
And some of me can kill a man.

I spring from rot and seed the earth,
The pizza and the soup adore me;
The toad's cap and the button both
Belong to me, the fungus fruit.
ciphers.hint: The fleshy, umbrella-shaped fruiting body of a fungus.

poem_stanzas:
I am a flat and golden round,
I sizzle in the pan and flip;
I take the syrup and the butter,
And stack in towers on the plate.

I am a thin and batter sheet,
The Shrove day and the lemon treat;
The breakfast and the dessert share
My warm and spongy, sweet embrace.
ciphers.hint: A thin, flat cake of batter fried in a pan.

poem_stanzas:
I am a mountain made of frozen sea,
I drift and loom and hide my mass;
The ninth part shows, the rest below,
And ships have died upon my face.

I calve from glaciers with a crack,
I am the cold blue wanderer;
The phrase for a hidden threat
Is borrowed from the sight of me.
ciphers.hint: A large floating mass of ice detached from a glacier.

poem_stanzas:
I am a ring of coral low,
Around a lagoon's bright eye;
The waves break on my shallow back,
And palms take root in my thin soil.

I am born of sinking rock and reef,
A necklace of the tropic sea;
The map shows me as a ragged O,
A garland laid upon the deep.
ciphers.hint: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon.

poem_stanzas:
I am the broad and sunken bowl
That gathers rivers to one sea;
The watersheds are all my walls,
And all the rain that falls is mine.

I hold the delta, hold the lake,
I drink a continent's slow rain;
The Amazon and Congo wear
My shape, a hollow of the earth.
ciphers.hint: A large depression that drains into a river or lake.

poem_stanzas:
I am a cliff with a smiling name,
A headland bold above the stream;
I hide no trick, but still I stand,
A wall of rock, a broken edge.

I am a boast and a deception too,
A poker face, a river bank;
The one who dares the edge of me
Pretends a strength he does not own.
ciphers.hint: A steep cliff or river bank, or a false display of confidence.

poem_stanzas:
I am the small and chattering stream,
I skip the stones and turn the mill;
I hide the trout beneath the bank,
And never rest, and never still.

A poet gave a poem my name,
I run to join the larger flow;
The poet heard my liquid notes
And put them in the mouths of men.
ciphers.hint: A small, natural stream of flowing water.

poem_stanzas:
I am a river made by hands,
I join two seas and lift the boats;
My locks are gates and stairways too,
And I am straight where nature winds.

Panama and Suez and the Great
Are dug and worn by me;
I carry trade across the land
And turn a desert green with ships.
ciphers.hint: A man-made waterway for boats, often with locks.

poem_stanzas:
I am the land that juts to sea,
A finger pointing from the coast;
The sailors fear to round my horn,
The sailor rounds me with relief.

I share my name with cloth and hero,
The headland of the continents;
Good Hope and Horn are mine to wear,
The last of land, the first of sea.
ciphers.hint: A point of land projecting into a sea or lake.

poem_stanzas:
I am a river's final fan,
A triangle of silt and reed;
I split the stream in branching veins
And build new land out of the mud.

I wear the shape the river draws,
The Nile and Mississippi wear
My name where they meet the sea,
A fertile marsh of shifting ground.
ciphers.hint: The triangular area of land where a river splits before entering the sea.

poem_stanzas:
I am the meeting of two waters,
Where river fades to salt and tide;
The brackish nursery of the fish,
The nursing ground of all the young.

I rise and fall with moon and sea,
I smell of mud and salt and life;
The city loves to build on me,
A half-way world of tide and stream.
ciphers.hint: The tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea.

poem_stanzas:
I am a valley drowned by sea,
A long and narrow arm of salt;
The cliffs fall sheer into my glass,
And waterfalls drop from the heights.

The glacier carved me deep and steep,
Then melted and let the ocean in;
My name is old Norwegian,
A silver road between the walls.
ciphers.hint: A long, narrow, deep sea inlet between steep cliffs.

poem_stanzas:
I am the throat of the cutting river,
A narrow chasm with walls of stone;
The thunder of the water fills
My dark and echoing, winding hall.

I am the Texas river and the Greek,
A narrow pass, a swallowed stream;
The adjective for stuffed applies
To those who eat until they choke.
ciphers.hint: A narrow, steep-sided valley, often with a river.

poem_stanzas:
I am a sea that bites the land,
A great and curving arm of salt;
The Mexico and Persia know
My name upon their sunlit waves.

I am a chasm and a wound,
A difference that cannot close;
The word for what divides two sides
Is drawn from my geography.
ciphers.hint: A large area of sea partly surrounded by land.

poem_stanzas:
I am a drum with strings across,
A round and ringing, twanging voice;
I came from Africa in chains
And built the music of the South.

I am picked with finger and thumb,
I sing of rivers and of trains;
The bluegrass and the folk all love
My bright and bantering, eager tone.
ciphers.hint: A stringed instrument with a round body and a long neck.

poem_stanzas:
I am the deep and lowest voice,
The floor on which the rest may stand;
I throb beneath the melody
And hold the harmony in place.

I am a fish and an instrument,
A clef, a man, a guitar too;
The singer of the lower notes,
The anchor of the tune and band.
ciphers.hint: The lowest musical range, voice, or instrument.

poem_stanzas:
I am the largest of the fiddles,
I stand between the knees and sing;
My voice is close to human sorrow,
And deep and warm and resonant.

I have four strings and endless grief,
The Bach suites are my sacred books;
I carry the sadness of the strings,
A wooden throat that weeps and sings.
ciphers.hint: A large stringed instrument played upright between the knees.

poem_stanzas:
I am the music of the clock,
The bell that counts the passing hour;
I strike the note and mark the time,
And ring in tuneful, sweet cascade.

I am a set of bells in tune,
I peal from tower and from door;
The wind can play me in the eaves,
A silver shower of ordered sound.
ciphers.hint: A bell or set of bells that ring in tune.

poem_stanzas:
I am a black and slender pipe,
A single reed within my beak;
The jazz man makes me wail and swoop,
The composer gives me liquid grace.

I am of wood and keys and cork,
I am the licorice stick of jazz;
I span the hollow of the wind,
A mellow column of the air.
ciphers.hint: A woodwind instrument with a single reed and a straight tube.

poem_stanzas:
I am the country cousin of the violin,
I scrape the reel and call the dance;
The devil is said to play me well,
And Nero played while Rome was burning.

I have a rustic name and voice,
The barn and pub and hoedown know me;
I am the same as the concert instrument,
But named for the common, homely hand.
ciphers.hint: A violin, especially when used in folk music.

poem_stanzas:
I am the coiled and golden voice,
The hunter's call, the call to war;
I flare in brass and bellow low,
And brazen means the sound of me.

I sit upon the animal's head,
I am a car's own warning cry;
I am the brass and bone and wind,
The curved and calling, ancient voice.
ciphers.hint: A brass instrument, or a hard growth on an animal's head.

poem_stanzas:
I am the song of solemn praise,
Sung slowly in the vaulted nave;
I rise from many mouths as one,
And lift the heart above the dust.

I am no ballad and no dance,
I am the music of the pew;
The ancient words and measured tune
Are mine, a ladder made of sound.
ciphers.hint: A religious song of praise, typically sung in worship.

poem_stanzas:
I am the woman of the fairy mound,
I keen and wail before a death;
My cry is heard across the night
And tells a household who will go.

I am the herald of the grave,
A washer at the ford of blood;
My name in Irish means the fairy woman,
The sorrow that foretells the loss.
ciphers.hint: A female spirit whose wail is said to foretell a death.

poem_stanzas:
I am the little king of serpents,
My glance can turn a man to stone;
I hatched beneath a rooster's egg
And rule the dark with poison breath.

I am a lizard of the legends,
A weasel's cry can be my death;
The traveler in the medieval bestiary
Fears me above all crawling things.
ciphers.hint: A mythical serpent or lizard whose look could kill.

poem_stanzas:
I am a beast of three in one,
A lion, goat, and serpent twined;
I breathe the fire and block the pass,
And fall to a hero on a winged horse.

I am a dream that cannot be,
A wish impossible and wild;
The scientists have named a gene,
And poets call a fancy mine.
ciphers.hint: A mythical fire-breathing monster of mixed parts; also an impossible idea.

poem_stanzas:
I am the giant with a single eye,
I forge the thunderbolts of the gods;
I herd the sheep and eat the men
Who wander to my island cave.

I am the smith beneath the mountain,
The one-eyed shepherd of the shore;
My father is the sea, my name
Is round of eye in the Greek tongue.
ciphers.hint: A mythical giant with a single eye in the middle of its forehead.

poem_stanzas:
I am the little man of the earth,
I guard the gold and mushroom ring;
I wear a pointed cap and beard,
And live beneath the garden lawn.

I am the watchman of the mine,
I turn to stone when sunlight finds me;
The garden statue at your door
May be my likeness, still and small.
ciphers.hint: A mythical dwarf-like creature said to live underground.

poem_stanzas:
I am a bird with a woman's face,
I snatch the feast and foul the air;
I am the storm-wind made of feathers,
The punishment of the prophet's hunger.

I am a scold, a shrew, a plague,
My name means one who snatches things;
The wind-spirits of the old Greek myth,
A screeching fury of the sky.
ciphers.hint: A mythical monster with a woman's head and a bird's body.

poem_stanzas:
I had a face that none could see,
And live, for serpents were my hair;
A hero used a mirror bright
To strike me down and take my head.

I was a priestess, then a curse,
My gaze could turn a man to stone;
The shield of the goddess bears my face
To frighten foes forevermore.
ciphers.hint: A mythical woman with snakes for hair whose gaze turned people to stone.

poem_stanzas:
I am the giant of the tales,
I grind the bones to make my bread;
I live beyond the beanstalk cloud
And smell the blood of an Englishman.

I am the monster of the nursery,
The one who eats the children whole;
My name is French, a frightful thing,
The fee from a darker fairy tale.
ciphers.hint: A man-eating giant of fairy tales and folklore.

poem_stanzas:
I am the mountain coming down,
A white and roaring wall of snow;
I bury village, road, and pine,
And wake the valley with my thunder.

I slide when sun and frost conspire,
I gather speed and loose my mass;
The skier dreads the slab of me,
The fatal river made of winter.
ciphers.hint: A mass of snow and ice sliding rapidly down a mountain.

poem_stanzas:
I am a rock of rounded bulk,
Too big for one hand to lift;
The glacier carried me afar
And left me standing in the field.

I am a stone the size of a house,
I sit unbothered by the years;
The climber loves my weathered face,
The geologist my traveled past.
ciphers.hint: A large rock, typically one rounded or worn by weathering.

poem_stanzas:
I am the promise of the leaf,
A folded green, a tiny fist;
I wait within the winter wood
And open when the warm wind calls.

I am the small and swelling knot
Before the blossom breaks to flower;
The spring is written in my shape,
The beginning that the garden keeps.
ciphers.hint: A small swelling on a plant that develops into a leaf or flower.

poem_stanzas:
I am a plant of thorn and water,
A barrel, a candelabra, a whip;
I store the rain in fleshy cells
And bloom a single night a year.

I have no leaf, but spines instead,
I guard the desert with my points;
The mouse and hawk both make their home
Within my prickly, patient arms.
ciphers.hint: A desert plant with thick fleshy stems and spines.

poem_stanzas:
I am a garden built of stone
By tiny mouths in shallow seas;
I make a wall that shelters fish
And break the sailor's wandering heart.

I grow one ring for every year,
My colors come from sunlight's friend;
The reef is me, the sea is mine,
A city built by living ash.
ciphers.hint: A hard, colorful structure built by tiny sea animals in warm waters.

poem_stanzas:
I am a thread of water small,
Between the mossy, shaded stones;
I am the sound of summer shade,
The place the children seek for frogs.

A different word for stream am I,
The small and winding, modest flow;
My name in British is a stream,
In American a smaller run.
ciphers.hint: A small stream or tributary of a river.

poem_stanzas:
I am the first and palest light,
The grey that drinks the morning star;
I bring the rooster to his cry
And turn the east from black to rose.

I am the herald of the sun,
The time of hope and waking birds;
The opposite of the closing dark,
The page the new day writes upon.
ciphers.hint: The first appearance of light in the morning.

poem_stanzas:
I am the closing of the day,
The purple hour, the first of stars;
I settle dust and dim the hills
And call the bat and moth to flight.

I am the opposite of the breaking light,
The troubled and the tender time;
The farmer leaves the field for me,
The lover waits, the lamp is lit.
ciphers.hint: The darker stage of twilight in the evening.

poem_stanzas:
I am the block where hammers sing,
A horned and heavy lump of iron;
I ring and shape the glowing bar
And turn the ore to horseshoe, blade.

I am the storm-cloud's name as well,
The cumulonimbus dark and flat;
The smith's whole world is built on me,
The weight and song of honest work.
ciphers.hint: A heavy iron block on which metal is hammered into shape.

poem_stanzas:
I am a bag of captured air,
I rise and tug against the string;
I am a round and bright and giddy thing,
And pop with sudden, frightful sound.

I carry men across the sky,
I make a party of a room;
And when a child lets go of me,
I climb and shrink and disappear.
ciphers.hint: An inflatable rubber bag, or a large aircraft filled with gas.

poem_stanzas:
I am a woven cradle of the hand,
Of reed and willow, cane and grass;
I hold the eggs and hold the bread,
And Moses floated to the Nile.

I am the hoop with handles high,
The picker's friend, the shopper's load;
The picnic and the harvest share
My open, woven, useful shape.
ciphers.hint: A container made of woven material with a handle.

poem_stanzas:
I am a bundle bound to a stick,
I sweep the hearth and clear the dust;
The witch rides me across the moon,
And Cinderella knows my work.

I am the besom of the old,
The yard and kitchen both are mine;
The new one sweeps away the year,
The teacher's rule is named for me.
ciphers.hint: A brush with a long handle used for sweeping.

poem_stanzas:
I turn the blue litmus to red,
I bite the metal and the stone;
I am the sour on the tongue,
And give the lemon its sharp sting.

I give a proton to the base,
My strength is measured on a scale;
The stomach keeps me for the food,
The battery needs me for its charge.
ciphers.hint: A chemical substance that reacts with bases and can burn or corrode.

poem_stanzas:
I am the element of life,
Four bonds to build a world of shapes;
I am the diamond and the coal,
The graphite in the pencil dark.

I am the base of every living thing,
I cycle through the air and soil;
My fourteen tells the age of bones,
And with two of oxygen I make the breath we give.
ciphers.hint: The chemical element that forms the basis of all known life.

poem_stanzas:
Within the throat a hollow bridge is strung,
Two folded cords that quiver when I speak,
I shelter breath before it becomes song,
And close to guard the road that food must take.

When a cold descends, my gates grow rough and sore,
A whisper cracks where once a trumpet rang,
I am the singer's hidden, hinged door,
The reed the air must pass to find a name.
ciphers.hint: The voice box perched at the top of the windpipe.

poem_stanzas:
Deep in the hardest chambers I reside,
A soft and fatty treasure none can see,
I brew the blood that floods the body's tide,
And nurse the cells that make a remedy.

An oxtail stew once coaxed me to the spoon,
A proverb says I reach down to the bone,
In winter I am warmth, and hunger soon
Will crack me from my cage to feed its own.
